prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the four-frame engine-flame loop of the KESTREL thruster — the small fire that flickers behind the hero fighter, drawn as one clear subject.

Design identity to keep exactly — a single solid engine flame-plume of horizontal fire about 1.4-1.8:1 wider than tall: one continuous tapered tongue of fire with real body, anchored broad at its nozzle mouth and flowing to a soft rounded tip. The plume is warm fire itself: a deep-orange body (#e84818) with a broad amber-yellow inner glow (#f8c030) and a pale white-hot heart (#fff8d0) at the nozzle root. The flame sits alone on flat key — no ship, no hardware, no smoke.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 4 cells laid out as a 2×2 GRID (2-column by 2-row, reading left-right then top-bottom) — every cell holding exactly ONE subject at the same scale and position; a missing, empty or merged cell ruins the entire sheet.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = FRAME 0 LOW BURN — a short stocky plume about 250 px long and 165 px tall, compact and rounded, its mantle sitting well inside the top border and its tip well inside the left border, on a wide island of flat key: mostly deep orange with a small amber-yellow inner glow and a pale white-hot heart at the nozzle root. The subject lies within aspect 1.20:1 to 2.10:1.
  cell 2 = FRAME 1 HIGH BURN — the SAME 250 px × 165 px plume at the SAME length and height, only brighter and fuller: the amber-yellow inner glow broadens across the body and the white-hot heart blazes toward the rounded tip. The subject lies within aspect 1.20:1 to 2.10:1.
  cell 3 = FRAME 2 SPARK — the SAME 250 px × 165 px plume flickering: a bright bead of spark-light swells at the nozzle root and the tail narrows a little — the overall drop keeps exactly 250 px × 165 px. The subject lies within aspect 1.20:1 to 2.10:1.
  cell 4 = FRAME 3 SURGE — the plume swollen taller at its base (250 px long, 165-180 px tall): a wide hot root with a broad amber-yellow mantle around the white heart before it tapers to its single rounded tip. The subject lies within aspect 1.20:1 to 2.10:1.
- FLAME GEOMETRY LAW: the flame-plume's NOZZLE mouth sits well INSET — leave at least 25% of the cell width (about 70 px) as flat key to the RIGHT of the nozzle, and the plume trails LEFT a SHORT distance (the whole flame is stubby, its blunt tip stopping 70 px short of the left border). The white-hot heart hugs the nozzle. All four cells share the same inset nozzle position, scale and vertical centre.
- SOLID PLUME LAW: each frame shows ONE continuous, THICK flame-plume — a squat, volumetric tongue of fire that fills 60-70% of the cell HEIGHT (155-180 px tall): a broad round nozzle root, a fat rounded mantle of colour steps, and a single soft blunt tip. The flame is WIDE IN BODY and SHORT IN LENGTH (roughly as tall as it is long — a compact mass of fire). Keep a generous flat-key border on all four sides.
- FIRE DROP LAW: every plume is one SMALL compact fire drop of roughly 250 px long and 165 px tall, centred inside its 384×256 cell with a wide even band of flat key all around it — the same modest size in all four cells. All four plumes share the same dead-centre placement: equal bands of flat key to the left and right, equal bands above and below, the nozzle mouth on the exact vertical centre line of its cell. Even the brightest frame keeps this scale: every drop is a green-surrounded island with equal bands of flat key on all four sides, at least 50 px each, in all four cells alike. Thick and compact beats long every time.
- SAME SUBJECT LAW: every cell shows the SAME subject, the same size, the same materials and colours, at the same position in its cell — only the named attitude changes between cells.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 768×512 px. Produce EXACTLY 4 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 12 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: every subject sits at the exact centre of its cell at the same scale and position as the other cell — only the named state changes.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — as much detail and inner structure as possible AT that low resolution, crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, letters, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, signature, blurry, anti-aliasing, smooth gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, drop shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell, cropped subject, subject touching edge
